_note: The Laniakea Supercluster (WS-5c, RFC-037) — the ~160 Mpc basin of attraction our Virgo Supercluster is one lobe of, defined by Tully et al. (2014) as the region where galaxy flows all stream toward a common gravitational focus, the Great Attractor. A SCHEMATIC, NOT TO SCALE (PRD-030 principle 2): the Virgo Supercluster sits at the origin as the 'you are here' anchor out on Laniakea's edge, the Great Attractor is the dominant central focus, and the other constituent superclusters/clusters are placed in an illustrative layout flattened toward the supergalactic plane (small z). This is a selected sample of Laniakea's named components, not the full roster. Distances (dist_mpc) + classifications are real; the xyz layout is hand-authored for legibility.
_provenance: Distances + types: Tully et al. (2014) Nature 'The Laniakea supercluster of galaxies'; NASA/IPAC NED; Cosmicflows-2 velocity field. Schematic positions hand-authored for legibility.
